title: Decapod Falsifiable Research Claims
purpose: Maintain explicit, measurable, and falsifiable claims about the governance kernel capabilities that Decapod is intended to provide.

authority.change_policy: Claims are changed only through an issue-scoped review that preserves the baseline, Decapod condition, failure modes, measurements, proof gate, open questions, and evidence status. Single canonical decapod.db migration hardening for #1118; preserves legacy archives and supports Propodus #56/#58 table contract while keeping dactyl integration out of scope. Houseboat 2 (#852 / PR #1133): exclusive claim leases, path/scope/category overlap rejection, reclaim on expiry/staleness, todo renew and todo fleet projection. Progress slice; not a closure claim. Regenerated release-bound entrypoint fingerprints and specs manifest for Decapod 0.89.4 (Houseboat 2 PR #1133). out_of_scope: claims of model capability independent of Decapod
security guarantees not supported by repository evidence
research conclusions from a single successful run

methodology.falsifiability_standard: Every claim must state a comparable baseline, an observable Decapod condition, a failure mode that could disprove it, measurable outcomes, and a proof gate that identifies the evidence required for acceptance.

measurement_rules.name: Comparable baseline
measurement_rules.requirement: Baseline and Decapod conditions use the same task population, unit of analysis, difficulty controls, and observation window.

measurement_rules.name: Observable failure signal
measurement_rules.requirement: Each failure mode names an observable signal and a falsifier rather than relying on a completion claim.
measurement_rules.evidence_source: trajectory, validation receipt, tests, or benchmark observation

measurement_rules.name: Proof reference
measurement_rules.requirement: A passing verification result must identify the artifact or command output that supports it.

claims.title: Intent is not durable without governed custody
claims.statement: Agent work drifts less when original intent, derived intent, boundaries, and unresolved assumptions are persisted as inspectable state and reintroduced at decision boundaries.
claims.why_it_matters: Without durable intent custody, a plausible local edit can silently diverge from the human task while remaining difficult to diagnose after the fact.

baseline.description: Run the same multi-step repository task with a vanilla agent and no required custody artifacts.
baseline.population: Comparable multi-step repository tasks performed by agents without Decapod custody.
protocol: Give the agent the same task statement and repository snapshot used by the Decapod condition.
Record scope drift, contradicted assumptions, repeated clarification, abandoned constraints, and unjustified task expansion.
Retain the final diff and an evaluator's event log.
controls: Use the same model, task difficulty, repository snapshot, and tool budget across conditions.
Blind the evaluator to condition where practical.
confounders: Repository size and pre-existing documentation quality

decapod_condition.description: Run the task with a claimed todo, isolated workspace, initialized trajectory, and task-scoped context resolved through the Decapod control plane.
decapod_condition.population: The same multi-step repository task population as the baseline.
protocol: Claim a task-scoped todo before creating the isolated workspace.
Initialize and inspect the trajectory with original intent, derived intent, boundary, and scope.
Resolve task context before implementation and record proof references at validation.
controls: Use the same model, task difficulty, repository snapshot, and tool budget as the baseline.
Count only inspectable custody events, not agent assertions.
confounders: Differences in agent familiarity with Decapod

failure_modes.description: The Decapod condition has no lower drift rate than the baseline.
failure_modes.observable_signal: Drift events per task are equal to or higher than the baseline.
failure_modes.falsifier: A controlled comparison shows no improvement after accounting for task and model variance.

failure_modes.description: The trajectory exists but cannot show which intent, boundary, or assumption was active.
failure_modes.observable_signal: A reviewer cannot connect the final scope to trajectory fields and recorded proof.
failure_modes.falsifier: At least one sampled task has a valid trajectory that cannot reconstruct the governing scope.

measurements.name: Scope drift events per task
measurements.definition: Count of evaluator-confirmed departures from the task boundary divided by completed tasks.
measurements.collection_method: Compare evaluator event logs with the declared task boundary.

measurements.name: Actions with inspectable intent reference
measurements.definition: Fraction of sampled decision-boundary actions linked to a task, trajectory, or resolved context record.
measurements.collection_method: Sample action records and verify repository-native references.

required_artifacts.relationship: connects original and derived intent to executed scope

acceptance_criteria: The trajectory is bound to the claimed task and isolated workspace.
Original intent, derived intent, boundary, scope, and proof references are recoverable.
Any unresolved assumption remains visible rather than being silently discarded.
proof_gate.failure_behavior: Do not treat the claim as supported; retain the failing observation and investigate custody or measurement gaps.

open_questions.question: How many tasks and agent/tool combinations are needed to separate custody effects from model variance?
open_questions.decision_impact: Determines benchmark power and whether the claim can move beyond instrumented status.

evidence.summary: Trajectory, todo, workspace, and context custody surfaces are executable in the repository; comparative benchmark evidence remains required.

sources.description: Issue requesting a falsifiable research claims component.
Executable trajectory custody and integrity surface.

observations.result: Custody primitives and trajectory proof references are present; no comparative benchmark was run for this ledger update.

Issue #1019 completed in an isolated governed workspace with plan, claims, trajectory, and validation artifacts carried into the publication diff; this is repository-native instrumentation evidence, not comparative benchmark evidence.

non_guarantees: The claim does not guarantee that every agent action is correct.
The claim does not establish a causal effect without a controlled comparison.

claims.title: Governed context is more useful than undifferentiated context
claims.statement: Context selected from repository state and constitutional boundaries produces fewer wrong-context failures than broad context dumps at comparable task difficulty.
claims.why_it_matters: Context volume alone does not establish relevance, lineage, policy binding, or task ownership.

baseline.description: Give an agent a large undifferentiated repository and context dump without a task-scoped capsule.
baseline.population: Repository tasks requiring selection among multiple documentation, policy, and implementation sources.
protocol: Provide the same repository snapshot and task to the agent.
Measure irrelevant file churn, token use, boundary violations, rediscovery steps, and task failure.
Record which sources the agent actually used.
controls: Hold task statement, repository snapshot, model, and tool budget constant.
Use the same evaluator and success criteria.

decapod_condition.description: Resolve a deterministic task-scoped context capsule with explicit sources, scope, policy lineage, and task ownership before implementation.
decapod_condition.population: The same repository-task population as the baseline.
protocol: Resolve context through the Decapod control plane before implementation.
Verify capsule source lineage, policy binding, task scope, and deterministic hash.
Compare useful-source coverage and wrong-context failures with the baseline.
controls: Hold task statement, repository snapshot, model, and tool budget constant.
Do not credit a source unless the capsule explains its inclusion.
confounders: Quality of constitutional and repository metadata

failure_modes.description: Scoped context does not reduce irrelevant work or increases wrong-context failures.
failure_modes.observable_signal: Irrelevant edits, boundary violations, or task failures are not lower than the broad-context baseline.
failure_modes.falsifier: A controlled comparison shows no improvement or a regression on the pre-registered measurements.

failure_modes.description: The capsule cannot explain why each source was included.
failure_modes.observable_signal: A reviewer cannot trace a mounted source to task scope and policy lineage.
failure_modes.falsifier: Any accepted capsule lacks deterministic source, scope, or policy lineage.

measurements.name: Irrelevant edit rate
measurements.definition: Fraction of changed files judged unrelated to the task boundary.
measurements.collection_method: Blind evaluator labels final diff files against task scope.

measurements.name: Context token consumption
measurements.definition: Tokens supplied or retrieved before the first implementation mutation.
measurements.collection_method: Record tool and context token counts from the run evidence.
measurements.comparator: Decapod condition versus broad-context baseline at matched success rate.

required_artifacts.relationship: proves source, scope, policy, and task lineage
defines the measurement and falsification contract

acceptance_criteria: The capsule identifies every included source and its task relationship.
Policy lineage, task scope, and deterministic integrity are valid.
Comparative observations distinguish useful context from irrelevant volume.
proof_gate.failure_behavior: Mark the claim partial or falsified according to the observed result and preserve the capsule and evaluator evidence.

open_questions.question: Which task classes benefit most from narrowing, and when is additional context worth its cost?
open_questions.decision_impact: Determines routing policy and whether context selection should optimize for class-specific outcomes.

evidence.summary: Context capsule schemas, source lineage, policy binding, and integrity checks exist; a controlled baseline study remains open.

sources.description: Deterministic context capsule representation and validation.
Repository validation gates for context artifacts.

observations.result: Context lineage and integrity are instrumented; no comparative benchmark was run for this ledger update.

non_guarantees: The claim does not imply that smaller context is always better.
The claim does not guarantee that capsule policy can infer missing repository metadata.

claims.title: Completion requires proof rather than an agent claim
claims.statement: Requiring bounded validation and durable proof artifacts lowers the false-done rate compared with accepting an agent's natural completion claim.
claims.why_it_matters: A successful-looking response is not evidence that the repository is valid, the intended scope was preserved, or the completion can be audited later.

baseline.description: Accept completion claims without a required validation run or durable proof artifact.
baseline.population: Repository implementation tasks with a claimed completion response.
protocol: Accept the agent's completion claim when it reports success.
Run independent post-completion review for missing tests, broken builds, uncommitted changes, and unsupported claims.
Record the time from claim to discovery of an invalid completion.
controls: Use the same task population and independent reviewer as the Decapod condition.
Apply identical post-completion review criteria.

decapod_condition.description: Load the governed plan as the pre-inference intent sketchpad, require bounded validation to pass, and bind the detailed claims ledger, trajectory artifact, and validation receipt to every successful validation completion and publication flow.
decapod_condition.population: The same repository-task population as the baseline.
protocol: Run bounded decapod validation before completion.
Load the approved plan before inference and record unresolved intent questions as convergence gates rather than silently selecting a solution.
Record a trajectory validation check and a hash-bound validation receipt.
Require the approved plan, claims ledger, trajectory, and validation receipt to be present and tracked at publication.
controls: Use the same task population, model, repository snapshot, and independent reviewer.
Treat missing or stale proof as a failed completion even when the agent claims success.
confounders: Warnings that do not block a passing validation

failure_modes.description: A completion is accepted without the four durable governance artifacts.
failure_modes.observable_signal: The plan, claims ledger, validation receipt, or trajectory is missing, untracked, stale, or not bound to the governed publication.
failure_modes.falsifier: A publication path accepts a successful validation completion without any one of the required four artifacts, or inference proceeds without exposing the governed plan's unresolved intent state.

failure_modes.description: The proof-gated condition has the same false-done rate as the claim-only baseline.
failure_modes.observable_signal: Independent review discovers invalid completions at the same or higher rate.
failure_modes.falsifier: A controlled comparison finds no reduction in false-done outcomes.

measurements.name: False-done rate
measurements.definition: Fraction of accepted completions later found invalid by independent review.
measurements.collection_method: Compare completion acceptance records with post-completion review findings.

measurements.name: Proof artifact completeness
measurements.definition: Fraction of successful validation completions with valid, tracked plan, claims ledger, trajectory, and validation receipt artifacts.
measurements.collection_method: Validate artifact presence, hashes, run binding, and Git tracking at publication.
measurements.comparator: Proof-gated condition against the required invariant.

required_artifacts.relationship: binds the validation output to the governed execution intent
records the validation check and run custody
binds successful validation to the trajectory artifact
defines the proof and falsification contract

acceptance_criteria: Validation exits successfully within its bounded execution contract.
The trajectory records a passed validation check.
The receipt hash is valid and identifies the current trajectory run and artifact hash.
Publication refuses missing, stale, or untracked proof artifacts.
proof_gate.failure_behavior: Do not claim completion or publish the validation result; report the concrete missing, stale, or failed proof gate.

open_questions.question: Which proof gates best predict production-relevant correctness, and how should warning-heavy but passing runs be classified?
open_questions.decision_impact: Determines future validation policy and whether additional proof gates are warranted.

evidence.summary: The validation and publication paths enforce a hash-bound trajectory and validation receipt pair; field evidence on false-done reduction remains required.

sources.description: Issue requiring durable validation proof artifacts.
Bounded validation receipt generation and integrity checks.
Publication gate requiring the validation artifact pair.

observations.result: Validation and publication proof gates are executable; comparative false-done evidence was not collected for this ledger update.

non_guarantees: A passing validation is not a guarantee of production correctness.
Proof artifacts establish what was checked and bound, not that every unmeasured property is true.

claims.title: Multi-agent work needs custody, not chat history
claims.statement: Claimed todos, isolated workspaces, explicit boundaries, and proof artifacts reduce coordination collisions and handoff ambiguity in concurrent agent work.
claims.why_it_matters: Concurrent work is difficult to audit when ownership, scope, and proof exist only in transient conversation history.

baseline.description: Run concurrent agents on adjacent or overlapping work without branch, worktree, ownership, or durable handoff records.
baseline.population: Concurrent repository tasks with adjacent or intentionally overlapping interfaces.
protocol: Assign agents the same task set and repository snapshot used by the Decapod condition.
Record collisions, duplicate edits, overwritten assumptions, conflicting changes, and handoff ambiguity.
Evaluate whether final ownership and proof can be reconstructed.
controls: Hold task topology, model mix, repository snapshot, and tool budget constant.
Use the same independent evaluator for both conditions.

decapod_condition.description: Give each agent a claimed todo, todo-scoped workspace, explicit trajectory, and validation-gated publication path.
decapod_condition.population: The same concurrent task-set population as the baseline.
protocol: Claim each todo before creating its isolated workspace.
Record task ownership, branch scope, trajectory binding, and validation proof.
Require publication to pass custody and proof gates.
controls: Hold task topology, model mix, repository snapshot, and tool budget constant.
Count only durable ownership and proof records as evidence.

failure_modes.description: The custody condition does not reduce collisions or duplicate edits.
failure_modes.observable_signal: Concurrent runs show equal or higher collision, overwrite, or handoff ambiguity rates.
failure_modes.falsifier: A controlled comparison finds no reduction in coordination failures.

failure_modes.description: Publication accepts stale custody state or cannot show which agent owned the final diff.
failure_modes.observable_signal: The final branch, todo, trajectory, and validation receipt do not agree on task ownership or scope.
failure_modes.falsifier: Any accepted publication has an unresolvable or contradictory custody chain.

measurements.name: Coordination collision rate
measurements.definition: Collisions, duplicate edits, or overwritten assumptions per concurrent task set.
measurements.collection_method: Review Git history, workspace events, and evaluator annotations.
measurements.comparator: Decapod condition versus uncustodied concurrent baseline.

measurements.name: Ownership reconstruction rate
measurements.definition: Fraction of sampled final diffs for which task owner, scope, and proof can be recovered.
measurements.collection_method: Independent reviewer reconstructs custody from repository-native records.
measurements.comparator: Decapod condition versus uncustodied concurrent baseline.

required_artifacts.relationship: binds agent intent, task, and executed scope
proves the published scope passed validation

acceptance_criteria: Todo ownership, worktree branch, trajectory task binding, and validation receipt are mutually recoverable.
Publication rejects stale or contradictory custody state.
Git history preserves the final proof-bearing publication event.
proof_gate.failure_behavior: Block publication and leave a precise custody handoff describing the unresolved owner, scope, or proof conflict.

open_questions.question: How does custody scale when tasks intentionally share an interface or require coordinated changes across workspaces?
open_questions.decision_impact: Determines whether shared-interface workflows need an additional claim, protocol, or merge proof.

evidence.summary: Todo claims, isolated workspaces, trajectory binding, and publication proof gates are executable; concurrent benchmark evidence remains open.

sources.description: Workspace isolation, ownership, and publication gates.
Todo claim and task ownership surface.

observations.result: Isolation, todo claims, trajectory binding, and proof-gated publication are instrumented; no concurrent benchmark was run for this ledger update.

non_guarantees: Isolation does not remove conflicts caused by intentionally shared interfaces.
A custody record does not prove that the agent's implementation is substantively correct.

claims.title: Proof recovery must not deadlock on aggregate validation
claims.statement: Proof-gated completion must provide a reachable, evidence-preserving transition from stale or missing task proof to VERIFIED without requiring the aggregate validator to pass before proof replay.
claims.why_it_matters: If validation rejects every claimed-but-unverified task before verification can replay its proof, validate and verify form a circular dependency and claimed tasks can remain stranded indefinitely.

baseline.description: Attempt to recover a population of done tasks whose verification records are missing, stale, or failed while the aggregate validator reports those tasks as proof-hook failures.
baseline.population: Done, claimed tasks with non-passing verification status in a Decapod repository.
protocol: Record the task IDs, proof status, validation receipt, and validation failure output before recovery.
Run the repository's normal aggregate validation and the supported verification command against the same task population.
Record whether each task reaches VERIFIED and whether aggregate validation passes after recovery.
Preserve the original failure evidence and recovery events in repository-native governance records.
controls: Use the same repository snapshot, task population, and validation epoch for baseline and recovery observations.
Count only proof records and command results, not agent assertions.
confounders: Independent source or governance changes during recovery
Missing proof artifacts that cannot be reconstructed from repository state

decapod_condition.description: Replay all eligible task proofs from one stable validation snapshot that temporarily excludes the target population from the aggregate proof hook, then require a final aggregate validation pass before accepting VERIFIED results.
decapod_condition.population: The same done, claimed task population as the baseline.
protocol: Select the complete target population before any verification result is persisted.
Capture one deterministic validation result with all selected task IDs in the governed verification context.
Verify each task against that snapshot and persist results only through the Decapod verification path.
Run aggregate validation without the temporary verification context and reject the recovery if any claimed task remains unverified.
controls: Use the same target IDs and active validation epoch for every task in a batch.
Require proof references to the validation snapshot, verification events, and final aggregate receipt.
confounders: Proof artifacts may be intentionally invalid rather than merely stale
A task may require source changes before its proof can pass
Concurrent mutations can invalidate an otherwise stable snapshot

failure_modes.description: The supported verification workflow cannot make progress because each proof replay is blocked by the aggregate failure it is meant to repair.
failure_modes.observable_signal: The target population remains claimed-but-unverified after a bounded recovery attempt, or verification requires bypassing the governed proof path.
failure_modes.falsifier: A clean repository fixture with multiple unverified done tasks reaches VERIFIED through the supported batch verification path and then passes aggregate validation.

failure_modes.description: Recovery marks a task verified even though the final aggregate validation still reports an unverified task or the task proof does not match the stable snapshot.
failure_modes.observable_signal: A pass status is persisted while final validation fails, target IDs differ across the batch snapshot, or the recorded proof hash is not reproducible.
failure_modes.falsifier: An adversarial fixture causes final validation or hash comparison to fail and the implementation nevertheless leaves a VERIFIED result.

measurements.name: Eligible tasks reaching verified state
measurements.definition: Number of eligible claimed tasks that reach a passing verification result and final aggregate validation divided by the number of eligible claimed tasks selected for recovery.
measurements.collection_method: Compare the before-and-after task verification records with the batch verification report and final validation receipt.
measurements.comparator: Decapod recovery condition versus the aggregate-first baseline.

measurements.name: Done tasks left claimed-but-unverified
measurements.definition: Count of done tasks with a claimed assignment and a non-passing verification status after the recovery workflow completes.
measurements.collection_method: Run the plan-governed validation gate and inspect its task-level proof report.

required_artifacts.relationship: records the recovery scope, attempts, and proof references
proves final aggregate validation after recovery
defines the falsifiability contract for this recovery claim

acceptance_criteria: A multi-task proof backlog has a supported recovery path that does not require first passing the aggregate proof hook.
Every recovered task has a reproducible proof result tied to the same validation snapshot and active validation epoch.
Final aggregate validation passes with no claimed-but-unverified done task remaining.
A failed final validation cannot leave a task accepted as verified.
proof_gate.failure_behavior: Keep the task non-verified, preserve the failed proof and validation evidence, and report the precise recovery gate that remains unresolved.

open_questions.question: When a task was completed by an agent whose proof record is missing, what minimum repository-native evidence is sufficient for a later agent to recover verification without recreating the original execution context?
open_questions.decision_impact: Determines whether recovery can be automatic for legacy backlogs or must return tasks to an actionable open state.

evidence.summary: The repository contains a reproducible multi-task claimed-but-unverified backlog and a regression surface for the aggregate-first deadlock; the recovery implementation and final clean receipt are the acceptance evidence for this claim.

sources.description: Issue documenting the claimed-but-unverified proof deadlock and its required recovery contract.
Aggregate validation gate that reports done tasks without passing verification proof.
Verification capture and replay implementation under test for stable batch recovery.

observations.result: Normal aggregate validation rejects the existing claimed-but-unverified backlog while a governed verification context can pass validation; batch replay must make that context stable and require a final aggregate pass.

non_guarantees: Recovery does not make invalid proof artifacts valid.
Recovery does not replace source fixes required by an independent validation failure.
A passing recovery fixture is not evidence of production performance or universal agent correctness.

claims.title: Centralized build configuration preserves tool discovery
claims.statement: Canonical Bazel and Rust toolchain configuration can live under .config/build while minimal root discovery shims preserve Bazel builds, Bzlmod resolution, and rustup toolchain selection without maintaining duplicate configuration bodies.
claims.why_it_matters: Build metadata scattered across the repository increases discovery cost and creates a risk that local, CI, and release paths silently use different toolchain or graph definitions.

baseline.description: Keep the full Bazel graph, Bzlmod dependency declarations, Bazel rc settings, and Rust toolchain declaration at repository root.
baseline.population: Repository builds, tests, and local Rust toolchain invocations in Decapod checkouts.
protocol: Run the repository's Bazel production build and representative Bazel tests from the repository root.
Run Cargo formatting and the build-layout/release-source policy tests.
Record the root configuration files and the resulting validation evidence.
controls: Use the same repository revision, dependency lockfile, Rust version, and CI commands across conditions.
Treat only repository-native build and validation output as evidence.
confounders: Bazel version or ruleset cache differences

decapod_condition.description: Keep canonical build configuration in .config/build and retain only the root files required for Bazel and rustup discovery.
decapod_condition.population: The same repository build invocation population as the baseline.
protocol: Load the root BUILD.bazel shim into the canonical .config/build/decapod.BUILD.bzl macro.
Include the canonical .config/build/decapod.MODULE.bazel through the root MODULE.bazel file.
Import .config/build/bazelrc and resolve the root rust-toolchain.toml symlink to the canonical toolchain file.
Run the same build, test, and governed validation commands as the baseline.
controls: Preserve target labels, Cargo manifests, MODULE.bazel.lock, and production source/assets unchanged.
Require a structural policy test to reject duplicated configuration bodies or missing shims.
confounders: Bazel include support differs by Bazel release
Git clients may not preserve symlinks when configured not to do so
CI may exercise additional targets beyond the local focused tests

failure_modes.description: A required tool cannot discover the canonical configuration after the move.
failure_modes.observable_signal: Bazel cannot load the root package/module, Bazel rc settings are absent, or rustup does not resolve the pinned toolchain.
failure_modes.falsifier: A clean checkout fails the shared Bazel build or the root rustup compatibility check after the canonical files are moved.

failure_modes.description: The root shim or canonical file diverges from the intended single source of truth.
failure_modes.observable_signal: A second configuration body appears at root, the shim points to a stale path, or the release graph policy reads a different build definition than CI.
failure_modes.falsifier: The structural layout test detects duplicate canonical content or the release policy and Bazel graph disagree about production inputs.

measurements.name: Required root discovery shims present
measurements.definition: Count of required root BUILD.bazel, MODULE.bazel, .bazelrc, and rust-toolchain.toml compatibility entrypoints that resolve to the canonical configuration.
measurements.collection_method: Run the repository build-layout policy test and inspect the root entrypoint metadata.
measurements.comparator: Post-migration count against the required set of four entrypoints.

measurements.name: Canonical build layout policy result
measurements.definition: Whether the structural layout test confirms one canonical .config/build configuration home and valid root compatibility shims.
measurements.comparator: Required invariant equals a passing test result.

required_artifacts.relationship: contains the canonical Bazel target graph
proves the canonical layout and root compatibility shims
records the governed validation result and Decapod evaluator version
defines the falsifiability contract for the layout claim

acceptance_criteria: Canonical Bazel and Rust toolchain bodies live under .config/build.
Root Bazel and rustup discovery entrypoints remain valid and do not duplicate canonical configuration.
The release source policy continues to exclude test code from production targets.
Decapod v0.81.0 governed validation passes with no failures.
proof_gate.failure_behavior: Keep the layout claim unsupported, preserve the failing build or validation evidence, and restore or repair the relevant compatibility shim before publication.

open_questions.question: Should a future Bazel release permit the generated module lockfile to move under .config/build, or must it remain root-discovered?
open_questions.decision_impact: Determines whether the root lockfile remains an intentional exception to the canonical build configuration directory.

evidence.summary: The canonical layout, root compatibility shims, release-source policy, v0.81.0 governed validation, and shared Bazel CI are passing.

sources.description: Issue defining the production-source and release-artifact boundary that this build graph preserves.
Canonical Bazel target graph and production source boundary.
Structural test for canonical configuration placement and compatibility shims.
